page: Microsoft Azure E32-16ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores. It provides 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high memory density of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include an x86_64 architecture with a 35 MB L3 cache and support for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES encryption instructions.

Storage configuration includes 1288 GB of bundled direct-attached local SSD storage designed for temporary scratch operations and caching, alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include discrete GPU acceleration hardware and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier performance across general compute and memory tasks. The instance registered a PassMark CPU score of 15944.59, a Geekbench multi-core score of 7729.0, and a Redis SET throughput of 13.8 million operations per second. Memory throughput reached 69.79 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 42.55 GB/sec on writes. However, single-threaded throughput shows lower relative efficiency, with single-threaded gzip compression achieving 23.83 GB/sec and medium 7B model LLM prompt processing reaching 24.46 tokens per second, both placing in the lower quartile of comparative benchmarks.

The constrained vCPU allocation relative to the 256.0 GB memory footprint yields qualitative cost efficiency for software stacks licensed on a per-core basis. The configuration fits memory-constrained workloads including enterprise relational database engines, in-memory key-value stores, large-scale ETL pipelines, and data analytics tasks requiring substantial RAM alongside fast local temporary storage.
